title: Autoscale governor: multi-metric reservoir controls and safety envelopes
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Design and implement an autoscale governor for Dedicated capacity that makes scaled decisions from multiple signal reservoirs (latency, throughput-per-GPU, request queue depth, error rate, and cost exposure) and enforces safety envelopes to prevent oscillation, runaway cost, and capacity starvation.

Context: Current autoscalers make scaling decisions based on single primary metrics or simple heuristics. As workloads diversify (chat vs. batch embeddings) we need a policy engine that: (1) aggregates orthogonal signals, (2) produces a stable recommended concurrency and replica delta, (3) respects hard safety limits and business constraints (min/max pools, cost cap), and (4) supports predictable throughput guarantees for committed Dedicated tiers.

Scope:
- Implement a multi-reservoir signal layer that maintains exponentially weighted moving aggregates and short-term reservoirs for: p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput (rps, tokens/s per GPU), queue depth, error rate (5xx/4xx), and pod-level utilization.
- Develop the governor algorithm combining: a PID-like smoothing controller for latency targets, a step/gradient scaler for throughput bursts, and a hysteresis-based tie-breaker when multiple metrics disagree. Allow pluggable algorithm modules for future ML-based policies.
- Safety envelopes: min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_rate_limit (replica/sec), cooldown window, budget-aware throttle (monthly cost burn guard), and cross-pool isolation rules (prevent scaling beyond pool quota).
- Integrations: metrics backends (Prometheus/OTel), runtime hooks for graceful drain and KV cache warm-up, Console feature flags for canary rollout of governor variants, and API surface to pin customer SLAs (throughput floor).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Governor produces stable scaling decisions in synthetic workload tests (no oscillation with step load and sinusoidal load for 30m).
2) Safety envelopes prevent scaling more than 2x beyond committed capacity without explicit override.
3) End-to-end e2e test that simulates a committed customer workspace with throughput guarantee passed for 95% of a 1h steady load.
4) Console shows governor decisions with causal signal traces and cost delta estimates.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prioritize predictability over aggressive cost savings for Dedicated tiers. That means slightly slower downscales and stronger cooldowns.
- Use PID smoothing for latency because it matches SLO control semantics; step scaling for throughput to react quickly to bursty traffic (e.g., large batch embedding jobs).
- We will expose algorithm knobs (gain, integral window, scale_ratio) behind feature flags before making them customer-configurable.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype multi-reservoir signal collector (2 wk): service-side library that computes reservoirs and publishes normalized metrics.
2) Governor core implementation (3 wk): implement PID+step-hysteresis logic, safety checks, and publish decision events.
3) Integrations and e2e (2 wk): runtime hooks, console traces, tests, and rollout.
4) Canary (2 wk): soft rollout to internal Dedicated test pool, monitor cost and SLOs, iterate.

Artifacts and links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Autoscale+Governor+Design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428, load-test script: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/infra/loadtests/autoscale-governor.

Open questions:
- What default max_replicas should apply for small-mid customers vs. enterprise? (PM input needed).
- How should committed throughput guarantees be enforced cross-region? (depends on routing policy).
- Do we allow customers to opt-out of cost-aware throttles for emergency scale-ups? (security/product discussion).
